sections.h2: What makes Round Rock a distinct place to sell a house?
sections.html:
Round Rock sits on Interstate 35 in south central Williamson County, roughly sixteen miles north of downtown Austin, and its housing demand is tied closely to Austin's growth and to Dell Technologies, which has its headquarters here.

The town began in 1848 on Brushy Creek, when a blacksmith set up shop. The name came from a round, anvil-shaped limestone rock in the creek, and the Chisholm Trail crossed the creek near it. When the railroad came through in 1876 the settlement moved toward the tracks, and the original site became Old Round Rock. According to the Texas State Historical Association, the 1970s brought dramatic growth as Austin expanded, and the population went from 2,811 in 1970 to 11,812 in 1980.

A seller should expect buyers who commute toward Austin, work at the computer and technology employers that grew up here, or want a house close to Old Settlers Park, the 570-acre park the city built with its sales tax revenue.

sections.h2: What is left of Old Round Rock's history, and does it matter to a seller?
sections.html:
Old Town is a small cluster of restored limestone buildings now surrounded by the rest of the city, and it matters if your house sits in a historic overlay area. The Texas State Historical Association describes the original site on the north bank of Brushy Creek as largely abandoned after the railroad was laid south and east in 1876.

The same history lists a Greenwood Masonic Institute opened in 1867, a broom factory, a lime plant, the Round Rock Cheese Factory that ran from 1928 into the early 1970s, and the capture of outlaw Sam Bass in 1878, which the town commemorates each year during Frontier Days. These details give the older blocks their character, and a house near them may draw buyers who value that setting.

The city's building page says alterations to a structure or site with Historic Overlay Zoning need a Certificate of Appropriateness before a building permit, and that applies to fences and accessory structures too. Preservation staff can be reached through the Planning and Development Services desk at 512-218-5428. If you are selling an older home, ask whether the overlay applies before you promise a buyer an addition or a new fence.

sections.h2: How does Dell shape the Round Rock housing market?
sections.html:
Dell is the city's largest employer and a main reason Round Rock can keep property tax rates lower than many neighbors. The city says Dell moved its headquarters here in 1994 under the state's first Chapter 380 economic development agreement, signed August 26, 1993.

In April 2024 the city council extended that agreement's end date from 2053 to December 31, 2099. The city reports it has kept more than $429 million in sales tax revenue from Dell sales for services and projects, and it says the sales tax revenue has helped reduce property taxes for decades.

A large employer base supports steady buyer interest, but your price still depends on your street, school zone and condition, so compare recent nearby sales rather than city-wide claims.

sections.h2: Which Round Rock building rules can surface during a sale?
sections.html:
A permit is not needed to sell, but unpermitted work can slow a deal, and Round Rock requires one for most work on a building. The city's building inspection page says a permit is needed for construction, alteration, repair, demolition and changes to electrical, gas, mechanical or plumbing systems.

  • The city runs a one-permit system, so related electrical, plumbing and mechanical work goes on one permit, and all contractors must be named on it.
  • A permit becomes invalid if authorized work does not start within six months.
  • Contractors and subcontractors must register, with no registration or annual fee.
  • Sheds under 200 square feet and 15 feet tall still need a permit as accessory structures.

Carports, pergolas, pools and similar structures are allowed only in side or rear yards, cannot sit over easements or setbacks, and are capped at 15 feet tall. Properties with historic overlay zoning need a Certificate of Appropriateness before a building permit. Call the Building Inspection Division at 512-218-5550 with questions about older projects on your house.

sections.h2: What does a certificate of occupancy mean for a Round Rock seller?
sections.html:
For a house sale it usually means nothing, because the city issues a certificate of occupancy only when a space is newly built, remodeled or renovated. The city's page says a new occupant who only makes cosmetic changes will not receive one.

  • The Fire Marshal's Office conducts annual fire safety inspections for new and existing occupants of commercial space, so this applies to a business, not a home sale.
  • If you converted a garage or finished an addition, ask the building office whether a permit was closed out.
  • Utility contacts the city lists for a move are Atmos for gas, Oncor for electricity and the city's utility billing office for water, so plan service transfers around your closing date.

The city also notes that the Williamson County and Cities Health District reviews food service plans, which would matter if you ran a home-based food business that you want to hand off with the house.

sections.h2: Can you rent your Round Rock house instead of selling it?
sections.html:
You may be able to, but check the city's current short-term rental and hotel occupancy tax rules first. Round Rock publishes business guidance on its website, and ordinances change, so ask the city before you list a short-term rental.

Renting out a house you are trying to sell usually complicates showings. If a tenant is in place, Texas requires written notice before an eviction case, and a buyer may want vacant possession at closing.

sections.h2: How do Williamson County exemptions and tax caps work for a buyer or seller?
sections.html:
Williamson Central Appraisal District values homes, and a homeowner's exemption removes part of the value from taxation. The regular filing period runs January 1 through April 30, and a late application can be filed up to two years after the tax becomes delinquent, per Tax Code Section 11.431(a), according to WCAD.

Round Rock homeowner exemption facts from Williamson CAD
TopicWhat WCAD says
Regular filing periodJanuary 1 through April 30
Late filingUp to two years after the tax becomes delinquent
ReapplyingNot needed unless the chief appraiser asks or you move
Buying after January 1Exemption can apply for part of the year if the previous owner had none
Cost to fileWCAD does not charge for exemption applications

Source: Williamson CAD exemptions page.

Texas also limits increases in a homestead's appraised value to 10 percent a year after the exemption is first qualified, and owners who qualify by age or disability can get a school tax ceiling. WCAD notes that a homeowner who has been receiving a ceiling can have it pass to a surviving spouse of 55 or older who applies.

sections.h2: What property tax deadlines apply to a Round Rock sale?
sections.html:
Bills mail in October, tax is delinquent after January 31, and penalty and interest start on February 1. The comptroller says the start is a six percent penalty plus one percent interest, and the penalty reaches 12 percent on July 1.

A homeowner may split the bill, paying half by November 30 and the rest by June 30. Because the lien attaches on January 1, the title company will pay the year's tax out of the seller's proceeds. Ask the Williamson County tax office for a current statement before closing.

sections.h2: What if the house is inherited, in foreclosure or tied up with a tenant?
sections.html:
Each of these has a Texas process that affects when you can close.

  • Inherited house: a transfer on death deed passes property without probate if it was recorded before the owner died, while a muniment of title lets the court order and will go to the county clerk when the estate owes nothing beyond real estate liens.
  • Foreclosure: lenders send a notice of default with 20 days to catch up, then a notice of sale at least 21 days before the auction.
  • Tenant: justice court sets an eviction hearing between 10 and 21 days after filing.

A title company can tell you what must be recorded before a buyer's lender will fund. Ask early, because probate and lien payoffs set the closing date more than the buyer does.

faqs.q: Is Round Rock a good market for a quick cash sale?
faqs.a: Cash buyers are active here, but the price offered depends on repairs and location. Compare a cash offer against a listing estimate minus commissions and carrying costs before deciding.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit to repair a fence before I sell in Round Rock?
faqs.a: Call Code Enforcement at 512-341-3329, which is the number the city lists for fence permit questions. Building permits and inspections questions go to 512-218-5550.

faqs.q: Can I claim a homestead exemption in the middle of the year?
faqs.a: Possibly. WCAD says that if you buy and move in after January 1, you may qualify for the rest of that tax year when the previous owner had no homestead exemption on the property.

faqs.q: When do Round Rock area property taxes become late?
faqs.a: After January 31. The state comptroller says tax unpaid on February 1 is delinquent and begins to collect penalty and interest.

faqs.q: Who pays to record the deed?
faqs.a: Usually the title company handles recording after closing. The county clerk manual lists a $5.00 fee for the first page and $4.00 for each added page, plus other clerk fees, so ask for the total on your settlement statement.
